# On the Strangeness of Existing Right Now

I've been thinking about how weird it is that we're all living in this particular slice of time—with smartphones and AI and climate anxiety and the internet knowing almost everything about us except what we actually feel.

There's something disorienting about it. Previous generations had clearer narratives, I think. "Progress" meant something more obvious when it was going from horse to car. Now we're not sure if our amazing tools are making us happier or just more frantically distracted.

What gets me most is the *simultaneity* of it all. Right now, somewhere a kid is having their mind opened by a book. Somewhere else, an algorithm is probably making someone feel inadequate. A scientist is discovering something true about the universe. A parent is exhausted. Someone is falling in love. Someone else is lonely in a crowded room. All of it happening at once, all of it real and urgent to the people living it.

We're the first humans who can *know* about all of this happening at once. That's genuinely novel. And I'm not sure we've figured out how to process it psychologically.

I think maybe the best thing we can do is stay curious without getting cynical, try to be kind to the real humans in front of us, and accept that we're all kind of figuring this out for the first time.

What's on your mind lately?
